cond_0001.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
At least one year experience
Preferred Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
Certified to operate crane and manlifts

Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements, then connect with your supervisor and team to clarify any weld specifications before starting.
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified.
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment.
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness.
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation.
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and communicate recommended repairs to the team promptly.
Clean and grind excess weld, slag, or splatter.
Clean, grind, or degrease parts.
Operate manlifts and cranes.
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor.
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0114.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
At least one year of experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
Certified to operate crane and manlifts
Preferred Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
cond_0114.encouragement_text:
6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder (candidates with less than one year are still encouraged to apply if they meet the other criteria)
Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0149.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
Certified to operate crane and manlifts
Preferred Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
At least one year experience

cond_0158.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with welding techniques and fabrication work.
cond_0158.responsibilities:
Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0158.requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent preferred
6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
Certified to operate crane and manlifts
At least one year experience

Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0167.requirements:

6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
Certified to operate crane and manlifts

High school diploma or equivalent
At least one year experience

cond_0224.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
cond_0224.responsibilities:
Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements.
Operate a welding machine to set amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse as specified.
Inspect welding machines, cables, and other welding equipment.
Determine the weld needed, position, and jig required per weld specifications and material thickness.
Guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining arc length and movement speed to achieve specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process to use for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation.
Examine welds for bead size, breaks, or cracks, and execute recommended repairs.
Clean and grind excess weld, slag, or splatter.
Clean, grind, or degrease parts.
Operate manlifts and cranes.
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor.
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Set up and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines such as brakes and shears.

cond_0232.intro: We are looking for a Structural Welder to join our team.
cond_0232.responsibilities:
Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grind excess weld, slag, or splatter
Clean, grind, or degrease parts
Operate manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0232.requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent preferred
6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
Certified to operate crane and manlifts
At least one year experience

cond_0257.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role. People usually become stronger in this kind of welding work over time as they build hands-on experience and learn from the work itself.
cond_0257.responsibilities:
Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0257.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
Certified to operate crane and manlifts
Preferred Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent
At least one year experience

Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0319.requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent preferred
6 Months to 1 year experience as a welder
Ability to pass weld tests
Knows and follows AWS D1.1 standards
Certified to operate crane and manlifts
At least one year experience
cond_0319.values: We value delivering results to a high standard and taking pride in work done well. We aim to be defined by quality, consistency, and strong performance.
cond_0319.workplace_support: We work to create an environment where employees feel supported, heard, and able to do their best work. Our approach includes flexibility, trust, and practical support that helps people thrive across changing needs and responsibilities.

Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0363.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Around 6 months to 1 year of experience as a welder, or an equivalent combination of education and training
Ability to pass weld tests
Familiarity with AWS D1.1 standards and willingness to apply them consistently
Certified to operate crane and manlifts, or willingness to obtain certification
Preferred Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent, or equivalent practical experience
Around one year of welding experience

cond_0372.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
cond_0372.responsibilities:
Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
cond_0372.requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent, or equivalent practical experience
Around 6 months to 1 year of experience as a welder, or an equivalent combination of education and training
Ability to pass weld tests
Familiarity with AWS D1.1 standards and willingness to continue building that knowledge
Certified to operate crane and manlifts, or willingness to obtain certification
At least one year of relevant experience

Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment, and communicate any issues early
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grind excess weld, slag, or splatter
Clean, grind, or degrease parts
Operate manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears. Stay in regular contact with your supervisor and team members to clarify job requirements and flag any concerns as they come up.

Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.

cond_0643.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp welding processes and how different materials and specifications come together.
cond_0643.responsibilities:
Read and interpret blueprints to determine specific welding requirements
Use a welding machine to obtain amperage, voltage, slope, and pulse, as specified
Inspect welding machine, cables, and other welding equipment
Determine the weld needed, position, jig needed per weld specifications and material thickness
Manually guide electrode or gun along weld line, maintaining length of arc and speed of movement to form specific depth of fusion and bead, as judged from color of metal, sound of weld, and size of puddle.
Determine which process should be used for moving raw materials or finished product in any given situation
Examine weld for bead size, brakes, or cracks, and make recommended repairs
Clean and grinds excess weld, slag, or splatter
Cleans, grinds, or degrease parts
Operates manlifts and cranes
Other duties as assigned/directed by supervisor
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products. Weld components in flat, vertical, or overhead positions. Recognize, set up, and operate hand and power tools common to the welding trade, such as shielded metal arc and gas metal arc welding equipment. Select and install torches, torch tips, filler rods, and flux, according to welding chart specifications or types and thicknesses of metals. Mark or tag material with proper job number, piece marks, and other identifying marks as required. Prepare all material surfaces to be welded, ensuring that there is no loose or thick scale, slag, rust, moisture, grease, or other foreign matter. Align and clamp workpieces together, using rules, squares, or hand tools, or position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises. Position and secure workpieces, using hoists, cranes, wire, and banding machines or hand tools. Melt and apply solder along adjoining edges of workpieces to solder joints, using soldering irons, gas torches, or electric-ultrasonic equipment. Grind, cut, buff, or bend edges of workpieces to be joined to ensure snug fit, using power grinders and hand tools. Weld separately or in combination, using aluminum, stainless steel, cast iron, and other alloys. Develop templates and models for welding projects, using mathematical calculations based on blueprint information. Repair products by dismantling, straightening, reshaping, and reassembling parts, using cutting torches, straightening presses, and hand tools. Ignite torches or start power supplies and strike arcs by touching electrodes to metals being welded, completing electrical circuits. Preheat workpieces prior to welding or bending, using torches or heating furnaces. Operate metal shaping, straightening, and bending machines, such as brakes and shears.
